The code does not explicitly check if `uniques > n`, but the logic of the method ensures that `uniques` is always less than or equal to `n` because `uniques` is incremented only when a new unique element is found, and it starts at 0 and cannot exceed `n`.

2. **ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException**: This is thrown if `fromIndex < 0` or `toIndex > a.length`. The code does not explicitly check these conditions, but `uniques` starts at 0 and is only incremented, so it cannot be negative. `n` is passed as a parameter and is assumed to be valid (i.e., `n <= elements.length`), but there is no explicit check for this.

3. **ArrayStoreException**: This is thrown if the value to be stored is not of a runtime type that can be stored in the array. In the code, the value is `null`, which can be stored in any object array, so this exception is avoided.
